d2c2e3: Ebook reader for Android: gestures instead of settings — Slowread
cb7496: Slowread: an Android reader you adjust right on the page of the book, no menus. EPUB, FB2, MOBI, PDF, DjVu. Free classics on the shelves and a gallery of masterpieces of painting with stories.
6cd02c: An Android ebook reader where font, size and color change with gestures right on the page. Opens EPUB, FB2, MOBI, DOCX, PDF, DjVu, TXT. Free public-domain books and a gallery of masterpieces of painting with stories.
532489: A reader you adjust right on the page of the book
6a1600: I love reading, though I don't always find the time. And I have never been against reading gadgets. I used to put ebooks together on my computer, load them into a reader and run them on a button-key Nokia. When modern smartphones arrived, I downloaded and bought subscriptions to a couple of reading apps at once.
88cfde: What I didn't like about them? There were a lot of settings, and I didn't understand many of them. I dug into the settings, changed something, left to see what came out, and went back in again. Now that I can make any app I like, I have finally got around to this.
de93f6: The first thing I focused on was making the reader as simple to adjust as possible. To change something, you shouldn't have to go into settings. You change it right on the screen of the open book and see the result at once. Need another font? Swipe sideways across the screen and the font changes before your eyes. Need bigger text? Spread two fingers apart to enlarge it, and a pinch the other way makes it smaller. A tap on the top zone switches your favorite themes, that is, background color and text color.
37b4f8: But that was only the beginning. I got into it, and made sure that the first time you open the reader, there are already books on your shelf, and free ones, rather than an empty reader or one with a bookstore. A welcome greets you, with quotes from great writers and masterpieces of world literature, prose and poetry from the public domain.
328e26: I did say I read from a button-key phone and from a computer. I couldn't always find the book I wanted online. Some rare books exist only as PDF, and often they are scans. I always wanted to read a PDF like an ordinary ebook, not struggle with an A4 sheet on a small screen. I managed it, as I did many other things. I won't write about everything.
fa71d5: I'll add just one more thing. As kids we collected postage stamps and Soviet postcards, and we loved looking at them. I, for one, studied every stamp, postcard or photograph in detail. Even the patterns of the carpet on the wall. It's something built into us, and that is why we never let go of our smartphones. I don't blame the younger generation for that: it's a marvel of technology. Anyway, I got the idea of repeating something like a stamp album, where there were often miniatures of famous paintings. That is why Slowread has a library and a gallery, with public-domain masterpieces collected by schools of art.
2c2513: Why Slowread, and why "Read unhurried"? Because fiction is to be enjoyed, not swallowed on the run. We are not the kind of people who keep rushing the user: the app has no reading-speed counters and no pressure. Read at your own pace.
f5aacb: In short. Slowread is an ebook reader for Android. Font, size and color change with gestures right on the page of the book, with no need to go into settings. It opens EPUB, FB2, MOBI, DOCX, PDF, DjVu and TXT. The shelves already hold free public-domain books, and there is search across Project Gutenberg, a quote of the day and a gallery of masterpieces of painting with stories about the paintings. The app is free, with ads at the bottom. No sign-up is needed.
777762: Swipe sideways to change the font. Pinch or spread your fingers to change the text size. A tap on the top zone switches your favorite themes, that is, background and text color. Touch the middle and drag to get your own color, not just ready-made presets.
858a55: The padlock at the top locks the look, so a stray touch can't change anything.
464256: Tap at the edge of a paragraph to add a bookmark. Bookmarks and notes on a paragraph are collected in one panel.
52c574: You can use your own font: pick one on Google Fonts, download it, open the file in Slowread, and your book is set in it.
edec3a: A typo in the book? Long-press by a paragraph and correct the text. Your edit stays on top of the book and the original file is untouched. You can save a corrected copy as EPUB or FB2.
032e49: The shelves already hold acknowledged masterpieces of world literature from the public domain, prose and poetry. The English shelf includes The Odyssey, Treasure Island, The Time Machine, The War of the Worlds, Shakespeare's Sonnets and Leaves of Grass. Tap a book and it's in your library.
68f66c: Below the shelves you can search all of Project Gutenberg in English, over 33,000 works. A card tells you about the book before you download it.
16eb53: You add your own books yourself: the app opens EPUB, FB2, MOBI, DOCX, PDF, DjVu (scans with a text layer), TXT, MD and ZIP archives of them. A book from your downloads, a messenger or a browser lands right in your library.
2ad743: The library shows real titles, authors and covers taken from the file, not a list of filenames. The table of contents comes from the book's own structure.
01a611: Which format to download: EPUB (recommended) or FB2. They hold live text that adapts to your font, size and color, and contents, cover, images and footnotes work as intended.
f58d08: A quote of the day: a new thought from a great writer every day, word for word from the edition, with the author and the translator named.
0f9729: A gallery of masterpieces. From ancient Egyptian painting and Song landscapes through the Renaissance and the Dutch Golden Age to Rembrandt, Hokusai, Van Gogh and Roerich. The works are collected by era and school of art. Each one has a story: where to look, the world it came from and why it matters. You can open a painting fullscreen and zoom into a brushstroke, a gesture or a barely visible sign. Gallery images load from the internet.
74a692: It is a reader, not a store. You add new releases and bestsellers yourself, and the app sells no books. The free shelves consist of public-domain books.
8ecea7: It is not a tracker for books you have read and not a reading-speed counter. Another app has the same name, so search Google Play for "Slowread" and check the icon and description.
8fe318: PDFs and scans don't read as smoothly as EPUB and FB2. With scanned books a lot depends on the quality of text recognition, and it can contain errors.
ea458c: There are ads from Google AdMob. There are no paid features or in-app purchases.
a35045: Your books stay on your phone and are never sent anywhere. Your reading position and bookmarks can be saved to a hidden app folder on your own Google Drive, but only if you turn that on yourself. Details are in the privacy policy. After you add your books, reading works offline.

103367: I used to work in television, in a newsroom. But that is not the whole point. I wanted an app that would give you urgent and vital news on the go. I pictured a news ticker running right across the screen of a smartphone.
aadbc8: It turned out you can't do that. Android and Google Play rules are very reluctant to let an app draw over other apps, and there are reasons for it: such a ticker would distract you, get in the way of everything else and drain the battery.
77910a: But once I started on notifications in the shade, I couldn't stop. I worked on the app for almost half a year. It is my second app after the counting app for kids, and it turned into a full news aggregator, in the same format as Bloomberg or Google News.
c903ae: It has notifications in the shade, a "News in one line" widget and the app itself: urgent and important news in a carousel, then live broadcasts and radio stations, press reviews on current topics, vital news (a power outage, an accident and the like), interesting stories and weather. And most important: we cover the whole world.
d4b451: In short. Ticker 24/7 is a news aggregator for Android. Urgent and vital news arrives in your notification shade and in the “News in one line” widget. Inside the app the news is split into three levels: local, in your language and world. It also has live news TV channels, radio, a press review, weather and exchange rates. No sign-up is needed. The app is free, with ads. Languages: Russian, English, Spanish, Portuguese and French.
6bcdab: A news ticker in the shade. Urgent and vital news arrives as a notification, and you don't have to open the app.
bbb79f: The “News in one line” widget. One news item, one sentence on your home screen, with stories replacing each other. Tap it and the full card opens.
e7a923: Three levels of news. Local: what is happening in your country. Your language: news from countries that speak it too. World: what matters everywhere. The sections stay separate, so you choose what to read right now.
70fd7e: Urgent and important in a carousel. The biggest stories are collected at the top, the rest below. The feed updates every hour, around the clock.
ff31f5: Vital news. Power outages, accidents and everything that touches your everyday life.
fd93dd: Live TV and radio. News channels play right inside the app, with no trip to YouTube: start one and keep scrolling the news without closing it. Each language gets its own channels. There are also news radio stations from your country and your language.
3a09a1: Press review. One event through several newsrooms: who reported it first, who added a detail, where the accounts differ. Every paragraph carries the name of its outlet, and we add not a word of our own.
5178e1: Interesting stories and weather. Interesting stories are kept apart from urgent ones, and there is weather for the city you choose.
6bb7ff: Full story inside the app. Read the whole piece without jumping to the publisher's website.
e274c3: Bookmarks, currency and crypto rates, dark theme. Save a story and come back to it later.
f57620: News is selected by one rule: is there an actual event behind it? Retellings of other people's opinions, ads dressed as articles and horoscopes stay out of the feed. We read every report. Spotted something wrong? Tell us and we'll fix it.
709925: The app needs an internet connection: without it the news won't update.
768c42: There are ads from Google AdMob. There are no paid features or subscriptions.
6a8b94: We show news, not official messages from emergency services. If you are in danger, follow them, not our notification.
20c7c7: The interface is in five languages: Russian, English, Spanish, Portuguese and French.
476d43: What the app stores and where it sends data is described in the privacy policy.

127349: Money tracking you don't pay extra for
20b8d4: For several years I used an expense-tracking app myself. I won't say which one, and I won't speak badly of it either. But it had a minus, and not the only one, but the most obvious: it was expensive. I don't know what the developers of such apps are thinking, but I got the feeling it was made for people who have money. That is, for people who have a lot of it.
6d0d38: Since I can do it myself, I decided to make an app for myself first. And, without false modesty, I wouldn't be myself if I hadn't come up with a couple of ways to make it even better. It is better not only because it's free.
532edc: Besides a nice interface, it has a lot of useful things: a built-in currency converter, statistics and comparative analysis, payment reminders and much more. In many similar apps such features come only with a subscription or a one-time purchase. Here they are available to everyone.
d7b3ab: In short. An Android app where you record your income and expenses. It has categories and budgets, several currencies and wallets, a converter, statistics and payment reminders. It works without internet and without sign-up. Your data is stored on your phone. Backups to your own Google Drive are optional and encrypted. You can move your data from another app with a file. Every feature is free, with no subscriptions or purchases. One small banner ad is shown at the bottom.
3fbe26: An entry in a couple of seconds. Pick a category in one tap. For regular expenses the app remembers your usual amount. The amount field has a built-in calculator: you can type 120+45 or 15% without leaving the card.
0fec3f: A wheel of categories. It shows the share of every category for a day, week, month, quarter or year. Swipe to move between periods; tap a category icon to see its sum and share.
2c14aa: Currencies and wallets. Several currencies and wallets, with transfers between them. The converter works out the amount in any currency: you enter the buy and sell rates yourself.
55d22a: Statistics about you. Where the money goes: essentials, hobbies and sport, little joys, the unexpected. Spending pace: this month against last month. What is still ahead this month, with a forecast. A lower balance threshold that the app warns you about as you approach it.
d97370: Comparison and budgets. For every category you see what went up and what went down compared with the previous period. You can set a monthly budget per category, and the app warns you at 80% and 100% of the limit.
07964d: Payments. Loans, installments, rent, utilities: what is paid, what is left and when the next payment is due. Regular income such as a salary or an advance is tracked too.
6003ff: Your own categories. Any colors, any emoji as an icon, subcategories and reminders. A deleted entry or subcategory waits in the trash for 90 days and can be restored.
857632: Privacy. "Icons only" mode is one switch, and nobody can read your spending over your shoulder. Unlock with a PIN, fingerprint or Face Unlock.
53d191: Moving from another app. Find "Export" in your old app, save the file and open it in Happy Pouch ("Transfer data / import statement"). CSV, Excel (XLS and XLSX), QIF, OFX, QFX, QBO and SQLite files work. Before importing you see which column goes where, so you can check it.
4cbaa2: Records and amounts live on your phone and go nowhere unless you turn on backups yourself. Backups are saved to the Documents/HappyPouch folder on the phone, and they stay even if you uninstall the app. You can optionally turn on auto-backup to your own Google Drive: the app only sees the files it created. If you sign in with Google, backups are encrypted with your account's key and won't open without it. That is also how your data moves to a new phone: a backup file opens from a file manager or from Google Drive.
f7c561: It doesn't connect to banks. You enter transactions yourself or load them from a statement file.
fb34e2: There is one small banner ad (Google AdMob). There are no subscriptions, paid features or in-app purchases.
242572: The interface is in English and Russian.
c053d5: If something is unclear, see the help.

1f081c: I wanted to download a calculator with a comfortable layout. That's all. I searched for a long time, downloaded a couple of dozen, and none of them worked for me. First came surprise, then fatigue, then genuine disappointment. At some point I waved it off and used the one that came preinstalled.
b94fdb: But nothing lasts forever under the moon. The age of AI arrived. I didn't jump in right away: like many of you, I spent a couple of years watching reels about neural networks and generated videos. Then one day I tried making an app with AI.
c4a0fa: The first thing I made wasn't a calculator but a counting app for kids: a ruler with a slider. You put the slider on 2, and to add 2 more you take two steps together with the child, and it lands on 4. I think it's a real leap for a child: they stop counting on their fingers and see right away how the result comes about. I'm convinced of that, though it's my opinion, not a scientific study. I'll tell that story separately. That's where my first steps in vibe coding began.
7c7744: So, back to the calculator. I didn't want to make one more just like the rest. I needed a calculator you can customize as far as possible. But that's not the main thing. The main thing is that it has not one or two screens but five. Why not? A PC can have three monitors. I could have gone higher, but I decided five was enough.
efce0d: Why so many screens? So you don't have to keep the result in your head. Swipe the screen aside, calculate on a new one, and if you need to look something up, swipe back to the first. In other words, it's a rethink of history and memory in a convenient format.
166e1c: In short. A calculator for Android. You can move, remove and add buttons, and pick the theme, color, font and sounds. The main difference is that it has five screens: calculate on one, swipe aside and carry on with another. There is a loan calculator, percentages, geometry, a converter and a home-screen widget. It works offline. It is free, with a banner ad at the bottom. The interface is in Russian and English.
6c3d14: 22 themes: light, dark and "electronic" ones with glowing seven-segment digits like old calculators (red and green LED, red and green LCD).
dae7e9: Your accent color, 5 button shapes, 7 fonts.
cb3361: Your own layout: move, remove and add buttons. Put + − × ÷ on the right or the left, which is handy for left-handed users.
b08330: Tap effects (ripple, rings, shine, sparks), key sounds and vibration. All optional.

f0229c: It started with a simple observation. Children learn from zero, and at first they all count on their fingers. I wanted to give them something they can see. A number line, for instance: the numbers stand in a row, and any operation is steps along it.
105ab8: How does it work? There is a ruler from 0 to 10. We put the slider on 2. To add 2 more, we take two steps together with the child, and the slider lands on 4. There is almost nothing to explain, because it is all plain to see.
1301bd: I think this is a leap for a child: from fingers straight to the logic of calculation. I'm convinced of it, though it is my opinion, not a scientific study.
c77a8e: Coming up with such a trainer is easy, but building it is much harder. It was my first app, and my first steps in vibe coding began with it: I made it together with AI.
fd6223: Over time we added a lot. Besides numbers up to 10 there are now tens and hundreds (up to 1000), negative numbers and decimal fractions. And we turned the ruler into a railway. That is why a little train is on the cover, and now it is the train, not a slider, that steps along the numbers. We added different backgrounds and music to keep children interested. And for correctly solved examples there is a reward: a new vehicle unlocks and confetti rains down.
bc3438: I also wanted the app to feel like a diary, not a textbook. So it has a welcome screen where the child picks a nickname and a future profession. From then on it is their own personal app, under their own name.
095647: We will be happy if even one child learns to count with the help of our app!
5ac37e: In short. An Android app that teaches kids aged 4–7 to add and subtract. A little train steps along a number line while the child counts the steps. You can start with numbers up to 10 and move on to tens and hundreds (up to 1000), then try negative numbers and decimal fractions. Solved examples unlock new vehicles. There is no sign-up and no in-app purchases. The app is free but has ads that are requested as child-directed. The interface is in 42 languages and follows your phone language.
b0b02a: A personal app. In the welcome screen the child picks a nickname and a future profession. All of it is stored only on the device.
b7b402: Learning you can see. Move the train and count the steps. When you see how it happens, the logic of arithmetic clicks much faster.
246f07: From simple to harder. Numbers up to 10, then tens (up to 100) and hundreds (up to 1000). For those who go further: negative numbers and decimal fractions, introduced through simple play.
f8aa06: Rewards. Solve a few examples and a new vehicle opens: a car, a tractor, a ship, an airplane, a flying saucer, a yellow submarine, a hot air balloon. Each has its own sound and leaves smoke or bubbles behind. A correct answer sets off confetti.
19d288: Vehicles unlock one by one. First after 5 solved examples, then 3, then 1. After that every vehicle is open for 18 hours.
8b1da3: Backgrounds. Drawn like a child's pencil picture: sky, house, notebook, space, sea, winter and a flowery meadow. Swipe to change them.
af8e13: Sound. Gentle background music that one tap turns off, and five step sounds to choose from.
d54e33: Comfortable. A dark theme for study at any time of day. Works on phones and tablets, in portrait and landscape.
d942f4: The app teaches addition and subtraction. There is no multiplication or division.
